$comment: Upstream container images this repository pulls, and where CI gets them instead.
LINUX/AMD64 ONLY. This is the first thing to know about the mirror and the
constraint everything else here follows from. The refresh workflow runs on a
linux/amd64 runner and copies the single-platform image it pulled there, so
these are NOT multi-architecture manifests. Pulling one on arm64 succeeds and
yields an amd64 image, which is why scripts/prime-images.ts refuses to run
anywhere else: retagging it as `alpine:3.20` would replace a working local
image with one that cannot run natively, and nothing would report an error
until a container failed for a reason that looks unrelated.
Making it multi-architecture would mean `docker buildx imagetools create`
rather than pull/tag/push. Not done, because the mirror exists to remove a
continuous-integration flake and CI is amd64; a contributor pulling from
Docker Hub locally is not competing for a shared runner address and is not
the problem being solved.
WHY A MIRROR AT ALL. Anonymous Docker Hub pulls are limited to 100 per six
hours per IPv4 address. This repository pulls six images per CI run and will
never exhaust that alone — the quota is spent by OTHER tenants sharing
GitHub's hosted-runner addresses. So the fix is not to pull less, it is to
stop depending on Docker Hub at CI time. GitHub Container Registry has no
pull rate limit for public packages.
WHY THE ORIGINAL NAMES ARE UNCHANGED. scripts/prime-images.ts pulls each
`mirror` and retags it to its `source` name before any suite starts, so every
Dockerfile, manifest and fixture keeps the reference it already had. CI and a
laptop run the same strings; nothing has to know the mirror exists.
A MISSING MIRROR TAG IS NOT FATAL. Priming falls back to the source registry
and says so. A mirror outage that hard-failed every build would be a worse
flake than the one this prevents.
ABOUT `id`. The image CONFIG digest (`docker inspect --format {{.Id}}`), not
the registry manifest digest — that one changes when an image is copied
between registries and so cannot verify anything after the retag. Being a
config digest it is platform-specific too, which is consistent with the
artifacts themselves. An empty string means the mirror has not run since this
image was added; priming still works, it just cannot verify.
